newsitem.title: GERMANY: German electronics sector sees disappointing 1997.
newsitem.headline: German electronics sector sees disappointing 1997.

text.p: Germany's electronics industry is likely to grow by a disappointing two percent in 1997 and shed more jobs in the process, Volker Jung, president of industry association ZVEI, said on Tuesday.

Industry sales are likely to grow to 230 billion marks, while jobs will "decline slightly" from the current 880,000, he said after talking with Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on how to promote jobs in the sector.
"These are not very good numbers in international comparison," Jung said, adding that the industry worldwide is growing six to seven percent a year.
Further cuts in taxes and non-wage labour costs are needed to foster innovation and investment in the industry, he said.
Rexrodt pointed to the recent completion of high-tech semiconductor manufacturing facilities in east Germany as visible evidence of the German industry's successes.

But the latest difficulties at Grundig AG are sure signs of the problems besetting it. Chief executive Pieter van der Wal resigned on Monday after Philips NV pulled out of executive control at the lossmaking consumer electronics maker.
Klaus Zwickel, head of the IG Metall engineering union, said the electronics sector lost 40,000 jobs in 1996, making a total of 200,000 jobs lost since 1991.
Rexrodt said demand-oriented measures and loose monetary policy were not appropriate to overcome structural weaknesses.
But he said tax cuts were urgently needed.
